questions.question: what do I get back when a fallible integer read finds the buffer too short
questions.notes: hard: all Buf::try_get_* / try_copy_to_slice return Err(TryGetError { requested, available }) (built in buf_try_get_impl); the infallible get_* variants call panic_advance with the same struct. Question shares no word with 'TryGetError'.

questions.question: how are two adjacent BytesMut halves rejoined without copying
questions.notes: hard: try_unsplit checks self.ptr+len == other.ptr, both KIND_ARC and same data pointer, then just adds len/cap; unsplit wraps it and falls back to extend_from_slice. 'rejoined' vs 'unsplit' is the vocabulary mismatch.

questions.question: where is hex (LowerHex/UpperHex) formatting for Bytes implemented
questions.notes: src/fmt/hex.rs implements LowerHex and UpperHex on the private BytesRef wrapper (write!(f, "{:02x}", b) per byte); fmt_impl! then forwards Bytes/BytesMut to it.

questions.question: UninitSlice
questions.notes: The public struct UninitSlice([MaybeUninit<u8>]) in src/buf/uninit_slice.rs is the type returned by BufMut::chunk_mut; it should rank first for the bare identifier.

questions.question: reserve
questions.notes: BytesMut::reserve(&mut self, additional) is the exported method a developer means by 'reserve'; reserve_inner is its private helper.

questions.question: who calls shallow_clone_vec
questions.notes: target src/bytes.rs::shallow_clone_vec. Verified call sites: promotable_even_clone (src/bytes.rs:1195) and promotable_odd_clone (src/bytes.rs:1284), both in the KIND_VEC branch of the promotable vtables' clone.

questions.question: what calls rebuild_vec
questions.notes: target src/bytes_mut.rs::rebuild_vec. Verified production call sites: freeze (bytes_mut.rs:265), reserve_inner (bytes_mut.rs:682), promote_to_shared (bytes_mut.rs:1136); also called from BytesMut::drop and shared_v_to_vec.

questions.question: what breaks if I change promote_to_shared
questions.notes: target src/bytes_mut.rs::BytesMut.promote_to_shared. Direct callers verified in source: shallow_clone (bytes_mut.rs:1161, ref_count 2, used by split/split_off/split_to) and advance_unchecked (bytes_mut.rs:1046, ref_count 1, when vec pos exceeds MAX_VEC_POS).

questions.question: how does BytesMut reach Bytes
questions.notes: BytesMut::freeze is the member of BytesMut that constructs a Bytes: it calls Bytes::from(Vec) (via vec.into()) in the KIND_VEC case and Bytes::with_vtable(..., &SHARED_VTABLE) in the KIND_ARC case (bytes_mut.rs:259-278).

questions.question: How does fmt parse a replacement field like {0:>10} inside a format string?
questions.notes: parse_replacement_field (base.h:1595) handles '{', the arg id, ':' specs and '}' for each replacement field; called from parse_format_string. Easy: name appears in question.

questions.question: How is the number of characters an integer will occupy computed before it is written?
questions.notes: hard: count_digits (uint64_t overload at format.h:1246, uint32_t at 1310) computes the decimal digit count used to size integer output; question shares no word with 'count'/'digits'.

questions.question: Where is the description text for an errno code produced, with a fallback if that throws?
questions.notes: hard: format_system_error (format-inl.h:1442) writes std::system_error(ec, message).what() and on exception falls back to format_error_code. Question avoids the words format/system/error.

questions.question: How does the memory buffer grow its capacity when it runs out of space?
questions.notes: basic_memory_buffer::grow (format.h:950) grows capacity by 1.5x (or to the requested size), allocates via the allocator, memcpy's and frees the old block unless it is the inline store.

questions.question: How does fmt print UTF-8 text to the Windows console without mojibake?
questions.notes: detail::print (format-inl.h:1752) checks _isatty and calls write_console (the _WIN32 overload at 1734) which converts via utf8_to_utf16 and calls WriteConsoleW; otherwise falls back to fwrite_all.

questions.question: Where is a multibyte character sequence turned into a single code point?
questions.notes: hard: utf8_decode (format.h:576) is the branchless UTF-8 decoder producing one code point and an error flag; used by for_each_codepoint. Question shares no word with 'utf8'/'decode'.

questions.question: hexfloat
questions.notes: format_hexfloat (format.h:3274, and the long-double wrapper at 3356) implements the {:a} hexadecimal float formatting; these should rank first for this keyword.

questions.question: utf8 to utf16
questions.notes: utf8_to_utf16 constructor (format-inl.h:1427) converts a UTF-8 string_view into a wchar_t buffer, emitting surrogate pairs for code points above 0xFFFF.

questions.question: who calls utf8_to_utf16
questions.notes: Target id: include/fmt/format-inl.h::utf8_to_utf16. Verified call sites: write_console (format-inl.h:1735 'auto u16 = utf8_to_utf16(text)') and file::file constructor (src/os.cc:219 'detail::utf8_to_utf16(string_view(path.c_str()))'). chrono.h copy_unit (1567) also calls it but is not indexed.

questions.question: what calls do_report_error
questions.notes: Target id: include/fmt/format-inl.h::do_report_error. Verified: report_system_error (format-inl.h:1455) passes format_system_error; report_windows_error (src/os.cc:165) passes detail::format_windows_error.

questions.question: what breaks if I change fwrite_all
questions.notes: Target id: include/fmt/format-inl.h::fwrite_all. Direct production callers verified in source: detail::print (format-inl.h:1760) and vprint_mojibake (format-inl.h:1748); do_report_error deliberately avoids it because it may throw.

questions.question: how does report_system_error reach format_error_code
questions.notes: report_system_error (format-inl.h:1453) calls do_report_error(format_system_error, ...); do_report_error invokes that func pointer, and format_system_error (1442) calls format_error_code (1450) in its FMT_CATCH fallback. Intermediates are do_report_error and format_system_error.

questions.question: how does Alamofire handle HTTP redirects
questions.notes: URLSession's willPerformHTTPRedirection delegate callback (SessionDelegate.urlSession#5, lines 200-212) looks up the request's or session's RedirectHandler and forwards to it; Redirector.task implements follow/doNotFollow/modify behaviors.

questions.question: where does a failed call get scheduled to run again after a delay
questions.notes: hard: gold is Session.retryRequest(_:withDelay:) which calls request.prepareForRetry() then perform(forRetry:) on rootQueue, using rootQueue.after(delay) when a delay is present. Question uses 'failed call ... run again ... delay' and shares no word with 'Session.retryRequest'.

questions.question: how is the server's TLS chain verified against files bundled in the app
questions.notes: hard: certificate pinning is implemented by PinnedCertificatesTrustEvaluator.evaluate (lines 258-284), which sets anchor certificates from Bundle.main.af.certificates and evaluates SecTrust. Question vocabulary (TLS chain, files bundled) shares no word with the symbol name.

questions.question: where is the HTTP body zlib-encoded before sending
questions.notes: hard: DeflateRequestCompressor.adapt (RequestAdapter) compresses urlRequest.httpBody via deflate() and sets Content-Encoding: deflate. Question says 'zlib-encoded'/'body'/'sending'; symbol words are Deflate/Request/Compressor/adapt - no overlap.

questions.question: where is the default User-Agent header built
questions.notes: HTTPHeader.defaultUserAgent (HTTPHeaders.swift:380-432) assembles the executable/bundle/version/OS/Alamofire-version string; used by HTTPHeaders.default.

questions.question: how does validate() check that the response status code is acceptable
questions.notes: Request.validate(statusCode:response:) in Validation.swift (lines 81-91) does the actual check and produces .unacceptableStatusCode; DataRequest.validate() (no-arg, lines 187-193) is the public entry that validates 200..<300 plus content type.

questions.question: multipart boundary
questions.notes: The boundary string for multipart/form-data is created by BoundaryGenerator.randomBoundary() ('alamofire.boundary.' + random hex); BoundaryGenerator also builds initial/encapsulated/final boundary data.

questions.question: RetryPolicy
questions.notes: Exact class name; open class RetryPolicy: RequestInterceptor in Source/Features/RetryPolicy.swift:29-340 should rank first over ConnectionLostRetryPolicy and the RequestInterceptor.retryPolicy extension helpers.
